items.title: 新浪时尚热点小时报丨2026年10月04日07时
items.summary: Sina's Oct 4 hourly fashion-trending digest frames Gucci's perforated/hole-pattern shoes (and Balenciaga's tape bracelet) as "novelty tax" purchases bought for social-media talking points rather than lasting value, contrasting them with asset-grade pieces like Hermes Constance or Chanel Classic Flap; advises shoppers to pay for resale-grade assets rather than novelty design.

items.source: Weibo (Gucci连放三个大招 analysis thread)
items.title: Gucci连放三个大招：首推中国制造运动鞋、降价超30%、Demna首秀，能翻身吗？
items.summary: Weibo analysis account thread asks whether Gucci's three simultaneous moves -- first China-made sneakers, price cuts over 30%, and Demna's debut show -- can reverse its decline; comment discussion splits between readers calling it an overdue correction to years of overpricing and others calling it "drinking poison to quench thirst" (饮鸩止渴) that cheapens brand positioning.

items.source: Weibo (古驰国内国外价差 FAQ thread)
items.title: 古驰国内和国外价差还有多少？降价30%-40%后买哪里最划算
items.summary: Weibo FAQ-style thread tracks how much the China-vs-overseas price gap narrowed after Gucci's 30-40% domestic cuts, concluding the China-market discount shoppers used to seek via daigou resellers has mostly evaporated; replies show sentiment split between shoppers pleased domestic prices are now competitive and resale-focused buyers worried the cuts erode secondhand value further.

items.title: Gucci cuts prices, but will Chinese shoppers return?
items.summary: Jing Daily reports Kering's "crown jewel" lowered prices across a selection of China bags and garments -- the Mercato small tote down about 22% to 20,000 RMB and the Ophidia mini bucket bag down about 29% to 8,700 RMB -- against a backdrop of cautious Chinese consumers who increasingly favor gold and wait for further markdowns rather than buying immediately, raising doubt about whether discounting alone restores demand.

items.title: 消费者对Gucci中国制造鞋的接受度如何
items.summary: Community reaction roundup citing Xiaohongshu comments on Gucci's Made-in-China sneakers includes skeptical posts such as one arguing 20,000 RMB could instead buy a trip with lasting memories while a Gucci bag just sits in the closet, and others recommending buying secondhand Gucci at half price instead; thread reflects a value-for-money backlash distinct from the production-origin debate itself.

items.title: 1000달러 구찌 신발에 '메이드 인 차이나'…무슨 일이?
items.summary: Korean outlet Asia Economy reports Gucci's Drip sneaker and a leather slip-on from the Primavera line now carry "Made in China" labels, priced around 800 euros/$1,000; Gucci frames the choice as reflecting the Chinese manufacturer's technical capability rather than cost-cutting, comparing it to using Swiss/Japanese suppliers for watches and eyewear, while Berenberg analysts warn of potential tension between the origin label and Gucci's luxury-image recovery push.

items.title: 140만원짜리 구찌 신발에 붙은 '메이드인 차이나'… '중국산 명품' 통할까
items.summary: FnNews' luxury-pricing column questions whether "Made in China" luxury can work for Gucci, noting the Korean retail price of 1.42-1.6 million won for the sneakers and framing origin as historically core to Gucci's Florence/Italy-craftsmanship value proposition; cites Gucci's roughly 50% three-year revenue decline as the pressure behind the move and flags risk that the label could further erode premium positioning.

items.title: "진짜 맞나요?" 1000달러 구찌 신발에 '메이드 인 차이나'…무슨 일이
items.summary: Nate News community-comment page syndicating the Made-in-China sneaker story shows reader emotion-reaction icons and a comments module typical of other same-day Nate articles drawing several hundred reactions; the skeptical tone of the headline ("is this for real") itself signals reader disbelief at a four-figure-dollar sneaker being produced in China.
